findings.title: Planning silently replaces a workflow that is waiting for approval
findings.observedBehavior: A committed-runtime plan command exited 0 and replaced a synthetic waiting-approval workflow with a new planned workflow, without an explicit supersession decision.
findings.expectedBehavior: Planning must preserve an active, paused, recovering, or approval-wait workflow unless an explicit reviewed transition authorizes its replacement.
findings.impact: The pending approval and resume lineage disappear from the materialized state. This is a local state-integrity defect; no unauthorized external mutation was demonstrated.

evidence.description: Committed baseline fd46d377183ea7efdc41317e064bb731568a7719; source anchor and offline reproduction active-workflow-overwrite.

findings.resolution: Read and reconcile the existing workflow/state before publication. Refuse nonterminal supersession by default; require an explicit operation-bound decision and append a valid transition when supersession is approved.
verification: Given a valid active plan and waiting-approval snapshot, new planning must fail without modifying the plan, snapshot, or accepted log.
Separately approved supersession must preserve the prior workflow identity, approval disposition, and a recoverable event trail.

findings.title: Planner emits new events that fail the shipped event schema
findings.observedBehavior: The new planner event lacks eventId, eventType, occurredAt, and payload and uses extra top-level fields that the shipped workflow-event schema does not accept.
findings.expectedBehavior: Every newly published event must satisfy the current event contract, with an explicit compatibility route for accepted legacy records.
findings.impact: Strict consumers cannot validate or replay newly planned workflows using the distributed schema. Existing legacy compatibility is not evidence that new invalid records are acceptable.

evidence.description: Committed baseline fd46d377183ea7efdc41317e064bb731568a7719; source anchor and offline reproduction planner-event-schema.

findings.resolution: Use a single trusted event constructor and validate before append. Put intent, step count, and state in the schema-defined payload; preserve legacy history unchanged.
verification: Validate every newly appended planner event against schemas/workflow-event.schema.json.
Replay its state with the shipped state contract and prove existing accepted history bytes remain unchanged.

references.title: Best practices for writing unit tests

assumptions: Reproduction data and transports are synthetic. No external operation or actual credential was used.

findings.title: Planner reuses event sequence numbers for accepted legacy history
findings.bugType: Physical-line count used as logical event sequence
findings.observedBehavior: Using an unchanged copy of accepted local history, the planner appended sequence 137 after an existing sequence 137. The accepted prefix was not changed; joined legacy records make physical lines differ from logical sequence numbers.
findings.expectedBehavior: A new sequence must follow the validated logical event lineage. Malformed, duplicate, or ambiguous history must fail closed or use an explicitly verified legacy anchor.
findings.impact: Replay and checkpoint ordering become ambiguous, and state can point to the wrong event. The reproduction uses committed code with copied accepted local history, including pending recovery evidence.

evidence.description: Committed baseline fd46d377183ea7efdc41317e064bb731568a7719; source anchor and offline reproduction planner-sequence-reuse.

findings.resolution: Derive sequence from a validated event stream or verified legacy-prefix/suffix anchor, not newline counts. Refuse ambiguous history and coordinate append under a single event-store lock.
verification: A joined-record legacy fixture must not generate a duplicate or regressing sequence.
Malformed or noncontiguous suffixes must fail before any append; accepted prefix hashes must remain unchanged.

findings.title: Failed inventory publication leaves a mixed report generation
findings.observedBehavior: A synthetic ownership collision caused inventory to exit 1 after replacing skill-inventory.json, skill-inventory.md, and skill-details.json, while preserving the previous skill-details.md and artifact-ownership.json.
findings.expectedBehavior: A rejected inventory must leave the previous authoritative report generation intact, or publish an explicitly incomplete state that consumers cannot mistake for a validated complete generation.
findings.impact: Consumers can observe mutually inconsistent inventory, detail, and ownership evidence despite the command failing.

evidence.description: Committed baseline fd46d377183ea7efdc41317e064bb731568a7719; source anchor and offline reproduction failed-inventory-partial-publication.

findings.resolution: Complete ownership and consistency validation before publishing. Stage the complete report set and provide recovery/rollback if any replacement fails; do not claim operating-system atomicity across multiple files.
verification: On a duplicate producer, all prior report bytes must remain unchanged.
Inject failures at each publication boundary and verify recoverable, generation-consistent artifacts.

findings.title: Caller transcript metadata bypasses the aggregate input ceiling
findings.bugType: Trusted supplied count instead of actual request data
findings.observedBehavior: The fake transport received two 5,000-character messages with transcriptChars: 0, although the configured aggregate ceiling is 8,000 characters.
findings.expectedBehavior: The limit must be derived from the submitted messages; optional caller metadata must not replace the authoritative aggregate calculation.
findings.impact: Incorrect or adversarial caller metadata can exceed the intended request-size/cost guard. Public attacker reachability was not established, so this is not classified as an exploited security vulnerability.

evidence.description: Committed baseline fd46d377183ea7efdc41317e064bb731568a7719; source anchor and offline reproduction transcript-count-bypass.

findings.resolution: Always compute and validate the aggregate from messages, validate numeric limit configuration, and reject inconsistent optional counts before token acquisition or transport.
verification: The reproduced 10,000-character request must fail before credentials or fetch are invoked.
Test absent, zero, negative, nonfinite, and mismatched metadata, plus exact limit boundaries.

findings.title: Provider rate records retain completed sessions without a bound
findings.observedBehavior: After 30 completed distinct sessions and advancing the injected clock by 24 hours, a new request left 31 session-rate records retained. Active identity records correctly returned to zero.
findings.expectedBehavior: Long-lived adapters must bound or expire per-session bookkeeping when sessions end or their rate windows expire.
findings.impact: Memory grows with distinct session IDs over the adapter lifetime even after request completion. No throughput benchmark or remote denial-of-service exploitation was claimed.

evidence.description: Committed baseline fd46d377183ea7efdc41317e064bb731568a7719; source anchor and offline reproduction session-rate-record-retention.

findings.resolution: Add bounded expiry/eviction or explicit session disposal and review similar circuit bookkeeping. Avoid replacing one unbounded structure with unbounded per-entry timers.
verification: Run many completed sessions across expired windows and assert retained bookkeeping has a documented finite bound.
Verify cleanup does not permit rate-limit bypass or corrupt active concurrent sessions.

findings.title: Retry telemetry reports one attempt after three transport attempts
findings.observedBehavior: Two injected 503 responses followed by success invoked fetch three times, while provider.request telemetry reported attempts: 1.
findings.expectedBehavior: Telemetry must report the actual number of attempts performed, including early success and exhausted retries.
findings.impact: Operational diagnostics understate retry pressure, latency causes, and transport work. This is an observability defect, not a demonstrated security vulnerability.

evidence.description: Committed baseline fd46d377183ea7efdc41317e064bb731568a7719; source anchor and offline reproduction retry-attempt-telemetry.

findings.resolution: Track attempts actually executed and emit the observed count rather than the configured maximum or a constant minimum expression.
verification: Assert telemetry for first-attempt success, one retry, maximum retries, and cancellation before another attempt.

findings.title: A stalled credential call outlives the request deadline and retains the identity slot
findings.bugType: Cancellation does not settle awaited credential work
findings.observedBehavior: With a deferred fake credential and a 5-ms deadline, the request was still pending after 35 ms and a follow-up on the identity failed concurrency-limited. It settled deadline-exceeded only after the credential was explicitly released.
findings.expectedBehavior: Deadline/cancellation must settle the request and release adapter-owned concurrency state even when credential acquisition does not cooperate promptly.
findings.impact: An identity can remain blocked beyond its configured deadline during token-service stalls; cleanup is deferred until the unresolved await finishes.

evidence.description: Committed baseline fd46d377183ea7efdc41317e064bb731568a7719; source anchor and offline reproduction credential-deadline-retains-slot.

findings.resolution: Make credential and other awaited pre-transport work cancellation-aware, including bounded settlement for noncooperative dependencies, and guarantee adapter-owned slot/timer cleanup.
verification: An unresolved fake credential must not retain an active slot after request deadline/cancellation.
Verify eventual credential completion causes no late transport call or unhandled rejection and that cleanup occurs once.

limitations: Hosted GitHub controls/alerts, remote-only refs, advisory services, package registries, cloud tenants, live providers, organizational policies, and fresh authoritative standards retrieval were not authorized or queried.
ESLint, a configured JavaScript type checker, PSScriptAnalyzer, and a local Bicep security/semantic validation result are unavailable; syntax checks are not substitutes.
No C#, Python, TypeScript, or other compiled-language application source is present in the committed baseline. Their instruction files do not establish native analyzer coverage.
Unreachable/pruned objects, forks, remote PR refs, hosted Actions logs/artifacts/releases/packages, issues/discussions/wikis, and caches outside approved local scope remain unassessed.
Manual analysis is trust-boundary and call-path focused, not a claim that every possible execution, concurrency race, browser/device state, or external service behavior was exhaustively explored.
No source remediation, installation, credential validation, cloud operation, commit, push, publication, event-history rewrite, or approval-state transition was performed.
The 26 pending worktree entries are separately inspected as deltas; the full gate applies to committed source only. Report outputs are the audit's permitted changes.

The full gate recorded 925 passed, 29 failed, and 4 skipped on Node 24.22.2/npm 11.19.1. The foreground terminal later resolved Node 26.13.0; one affected case and standalone verification passed there. Runtime drift was observed, but the null subprocess statuses were not conclusively diagnosed or treated as source defects.
This audit's reviewed-analysis phase does not replace the independently authored security-review approval required by the formal release policy.
